title: Twelve Thousand Stadia Definition
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the angel measures the city with a golden reed, and the measure given is 12,000 stadia for the city.
engineering: Engineering view: 12,000 stadia is a text-faithful figure whose physical length depends on which stadion is meant. This record defines the figure, preserves the alternatives, and refuses to settle the conversion silently.
body:
Public measurement scholarship lists several stadion lengths: the Attic stadion near 177-178 m, the Roman stadion near 185 m, shorter and longer regional variants near 157 m and 192-210 m.

The companion measurement-scale pair carries the full conversion method and worked examples; this record holds the definition itself.

demo.code:
TITLE = 'Twelve Thousand Stadia Definition'


def main():
    print(TITLE + ' - working demo')
    stadia = 12000
    options = [('Attic stadion, short', 157), ('Common stadion', 178), ('Provisional stadion', 185), ('Roman stadion', 192), ('Long stadion', 210)]
    for name, metres in options:
        print('%s: %d stadia x %d m = %s km' % (name, stadia, metres, format(stadia * metres / 1000.0, ',.0f')))
    print('NOTE: alternatives preserved; no single value is settled.')


main()
demo.expected_output:
Twelve Thousand Stadia Definition - working demo
Attic stadion, short: 12000 stadia x 157 m = 1,884 km
Common stadion: 12000 stadia x 178 m = 2,136 km
Provisional stadion: 12000 stadia x 185 m = 2,220 km
Roman stadion: 12000 stadia x 192 m = 2,304 km
Long stadion: 12000 stadia x 210 m = 2,520 km
NOTE: alternatives preserved; no single value is settled.

title: Length Equals Width Equals Height
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the city lies four-square, and its length and width and height are equal — a cube, not a flat plan.
engineering: Engineering view: length equals width equals height is a geometric constraint, and the cube model enforces it at every scale. It says nothing by itself about structure, materials, or habitability, and this record claims nothing beyond the geometry.
body:
Public geometry practice enforces equal-side constraints in parametric models, where changing one side updates the other two, keeping the cube a cube through every revision.

The demo computes volume and surface from one side, showing that both follow from the single equal-side figure.

demo.code:

def main():

    side_km = 2220
    volume = side_km ** 3
    surface = 6 * side_km ** 2
    print('Side (ILLUSTRATIVE only): ' + str(side_km) + ' km')
    print('Volume: ' + str(side_km) + '^3 = ' + format(volume, ',') + ' cubic km')
    print('Surface: 6 x ' + str(side_km) + '^2 = ' + format(surface, ',') + ' square km')
    print('Faces: 6; edges: 12; vertices: 8')


main()

engineering: Engineering view: 144 cubits is a wall measure whose physical length depends on which cubit is meant, and whose relation to the city is itself an interpretation question — wall height, wall thickness, or another dimension are all readings that have been proposed, and none is settled here.
body:
Public cubit scholarship lists the short cubit near 0.4445 m, the common cubit near 0.4572 m, the royal cubit near 0.525 m, and longer variants near 0.555 m.

The demo converts 144 cubits under each alternative, so the spread of possible wall measures is visible rather than hidden behind one number.

title: Two Thousand Two Hundred Twenty Kilometres Illustrative Conversion
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the illustrative conversion takes the provisional 185 m stadion times 12,000 stadia, giving about 2,220 km per side, as a way to picture the scale.
engineering: Engineering view: 2,220 km is ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY, never a settled measurement. It follows arithmetically from one provisional alternative, and it changes with every other alternative. Any figure downstream of it — volume, surface, proportions — inherits the same illustrative status.
body:
Public arithmetic for the illustration is simple and checkable: 12,000 times 185 m equals 2,220,000 m, which equals 2,220 km.

Under the other alternatives the same computation gives about 1,884 km, 2,136 km, 2,304 km, and 2,520 km, which is why no single figure is settled.

engineering: Engineering view: scale-aware modeling is demonstrated practice. A full-scale mathematical model holds the exact figures, an overview model holds the city at a navigable size, and a physical mock-up holds touchable pieces, with a scale manager stating what each scale can answer.
body:
Public scale practice includes full-scale mathematical models, overview and district models at stated ratios, and physical mock-ups with stated scales, all linked to one parametric specification.

The demo converts the illustrative full measure to overview-model sizes and to a mock-up ratio, so scale claims are arithmetic.

engineering: Engineering view: volume and surface computation is demonstrated arithmetic. Given a side, volume is side cubed and surface is six times side squared, and both are recomputed per stadion alternative rather than stated once for the illustrative figure alone.
body:

title: Full-Scale Structural Infeasibility
text_faithful: Text-faithful view (faith interpretation): the visionary city stands by divine making, not by human structure, and this record honors that distinction by refusing to dress a full-scale human build as feasible.
engineering: Engineering view: full-scale structural realization of a 2,220 km cube city is NOT ESTABLISHED. No known structural system, material, foundation, or construction method supports a structure at that scale, and this record labels the full-scale physical build not-established rather than softening it into a future promise.
body:
Public structural practice gives the reasons plainly: material strength limits, self-weight scaling, foundation bearing limits, thermal movement, and construction logistics all fail long before city scale.

What is feasible is the model, the overview, and the mock-up — and those are the scales this suite builds at.

demo.code:

engineering: Engineering view: wall-to-city proportion is demonstrated arithmetic. The wall measure under each cubit alternative is divided by the illustrative city side, giving a tiny percentage that makes the scale relationship visible instead of rhetorical.
